description:
FILED s516a (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-12), found by member 3's IO::Dir probe once the detector announced by default.

SILENT WRONG: `use File::stat;` does not displace the built-in stat / lstat at the PARSE.
    use File::stat; my $s = lstat("/etc"); print ref($s), "\n";   # perl: File::stat   PCL: (empty -- the built-in's list)
`&lstat(...)` works (a user call).  The detector (default announce since s516a) reports each site correctly:
"'main::lstat' was parsed as the built-in but code that ran at line 1 installed a sub with prototype ($)".
Core IO::Dir (`use File::stat;` + `&lstat(...)` in FETCH, IO/Dir.pm line 117) prints one such line per process -- a FALSE alarm there (the & call ignores prototypes; its table entry should not be "builtin" -- see below).

CAUSE: Pl::Parser::_extract_module_prototypes skips every `File::` module but File::Spec by NAME (cost), so File::stat has no env: no @EXPORT, so the builtin-override recorder records nothing.
TRIED (s516a, set aside -- scratch/s516a/stat-overlay-draft.pm in the s516a worktree): a facts overlay lib/PCL/Facts/File/stat.pm (`sub stat ($); sub lstat ($);` + @EXPORT/@EXPORT_OK/%EXPORT_TAGS).  The parse then reads the import, BUT the module load DIES: "PCL: facts overlay conflict for File::stat::lstat: ... overlay declares ($) but .../File/stat.pm declares ()" -- the real module writes `sub lstat :prototype($) { ... }`, and the conflict check (or the module scan) reads that ATTRIBUTE-form prototype as () .  That reading is the first thing to probe (does the module's own record say () for an attribute prototype?  a SILENT WRONG of its own if a call site ever used it).

SECOND HALF: an `&NAME(...)` call site is recorded in the detector table by the prototype lookup like any other (here "builtin"); an & call ignores prototypes, so it can never be mis-parsed -- it should not be a table entry at all (one predicate in Environment::_detect_note's caller, the force_user_sub path).

Guard when fixed: list + scalar `lstat` / `stat` under `use File::stat;`, perl-compared, and no PCL: line on stderr for core IO::Dir->new(DIR)->read.

=== PARTLY DONE (s516a) ===
HALF 2 DONE (c9251ff2): gen_funcall_form asks NO prototype for a force_user_sub (&NAME(...)) call -- perl ignores it there.  This was ALSO a silent wrong: main passed &f(@a) under sub f (\@) as \@a.  The IO::Dir false alarm is gone (guard glob-override-01.t rows 11-12).  HALF 1 (use File::stat; displaces nothing at the parse; the overlay's attribute-prototype conflict) is OPEN.
subject: use File::stat; does not displace stat/lstat at the parse (File:: modules skipped by name; an overlay trips an attribute-prototype conflict read as ()), and an &NAME() site is a detector table entry
